input.chief_complaint: 58-year-old established patient with longstanding type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease stage 3 presents for pre-operative clearance of an acute, symptomatic right inguinal hernia reducible for 2 weeks.

history_items.text: Right inguinal bulge noticed 2 weeks ago while lifting; reducible, no skin changes, no overlying erythema, no femoral bulge on contralateral exam.
Home blood glucose logs averaging 140-160; metformin 1000 mg BID continued; lisinopril 20 mg daily continued.
Last HbA1c 7.4 (3 months ago); most recent creatinine 1.6 (baseline 1.5-1.7).
Denies chest pain, shortness of breath, dysuria, fever, abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting.
Endocrine: no polyuria, polydipsia, polyphagia, or unintentional weight loss in the last 3 months.
Cardiovascular: no palpitations, edema, orthopnea, or PND.
Past surgical history: appendectomy 1998, no complications.
Family history significant for type 2 diabetes (father) and coronary artery disease (mother, age 65 stent).
Social history: former smoker (quit 2010, 20 pack-years), drinks 1-2 beers/week, works as an accountant.

diagnosis_codes.description: Unilateral inguinal hernia, without obstruction or gangrene, not specified as recurrent

expected_output.mdm_rationale: High complexity. Two stable chronic illnesses (type 2 diabetes, CKD stage 3) plus one acute surgical problem (right inguinal hernia requiring repair). Data review is extensive: home glucose logs, prior HbA1c, baseline creatinine, surgical history, family history, social history. Risk of complications is high — diabetic patient with CKD stage 3 undergoing general anesthesia for a 90-day global-period procedure; risk of perioperative AKI, hyperglycemia, and infection requires medication review and dose adjustment. Pre-operative clearance includes separate evaluation and management of the chronic conditions beyond the surgical indication, which supports a separately identifiable E/M with modifier -25.

code_selection.rationale: Established patient, moderate-to-high MDM with two stable chronic illnesses and one acute surgical problem, plus pre-op medication review for metformin and lisinopril in the setting of CKD stage 3. Modifier -25 is required because the E/M is on the same day as a procedure with a 90-day global period (49505, open inguinal hernia repair) and the E/M is separately identifiable from the pre-op surgical workup.

Open repair of inguinal hernia, age 5 and over; reducible unilateral right inguinal hernia without obstruction or gangrene. Carries a 90-day global period per CMS. Diagnosis K40.90 supports medical necessity.
